newsitem.title: PERU: Peru hostages still hold rich haul of VIPs.
newsitem.headline: Peru hostages still hold rich haul of VIPs.

text.p: Even after releasing most of their captives, Marxist gunmen holding the Japanese embassy residence in Peru still several high-ranking officials to use as bargaining chips.
The Red Cross said the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels are holding "just over 140" captives but it did not give an exact number or detailed nationalities.
About 80 of those held are top Peruvians, while some 60 are foreigners, local news media reported on Tuesday.

High-ranking Peruvian hostages are the largest group. The guerrillas are holding two cabinet ministers, five Supreme Court judges, five government congressmen, 11 senior officials and three business chiefs.

But perhaps their biggest prizes are the present and former chiefs of the DINCOTE anti-terrorist police charged with pursuing the MRTA and several generals and colonels from the army, air force and presidential guard.
Among the foreigners the Japanese are by far the biggest group, with about 35 businessmen and 17 diplomats and embassy staff among the captives, newspaper El Comercio reported.

From other nations, seven ambassadors are inside the besieged residence: the envoys of Japan, Malaysia, Bolivia, Honduras, Guatemala, Uruguay and the Dominican Republic. Argentina's consul-general is also being held.
